references.text: 1 John refers directly to Cain as the evil one who killed his brother.
Hebrews mentions Abel's righteous offering, which indirectly references his relationship with Cain and why Cain killed him.
Jesus refers to the righteous blood of Abel as the first innocent blood shed, linking it directly to Cain's murder.
Jude warns against those who have gone 'the way of Cain,' a reference to Cain's evil and his killing of Abel.
Lamek speaks about killing a man who has wounded him, which mirrors and escalates Cain's violent act against Abel.
After the flood, God establishes a law against murder—'whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed'—which reflects back on Cain's sin.
